sections.content: If you are searching for real estate deals in Moreno Valley CA, you have landed on one of the Inland Empire's most underrated investment markets. Located in Riverside County, Moreno Valley sits about 60 miles east of Los Angeles and has quietly built a reputation as a go-to spot for investors who want California real estate without the jaw-dropping price tags. Whether you are just getting started or expanding a portfolio, this guide covers everything you need to know — from current home prices and top neighborhoods to deal types and practical tips for out-of-state investors. If you are brand new to this game, bookmark the Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide at AIWholesail before diving in.
Moreno Valley CA Market Overview

Moreno Valley is California's 15th largest city, home to roughly 215,000 residents. It borders the city of Riverside to the west and Perris to the south, putting it squarely in the heart of the Inland Empire. The city has been growing steadily for over a decade, driven by affordable housing compared to coastal cities, strong warehouse and logistics employment (Amazon has a massive fulfillment center here), and easy freeway access via the 60 and 215 corridors. That combination of jobs, population growth, and relative affordability makes it one of the more attractive markets for buy-and-hold investors and wholesalers in Southern California.
Average Home Prices in Moreno Valley

As of 2024, the median home price in Moreno Valley sits around $460,000 to $490,000. That is a significant jump from the $320,000 range seen in 2020, reflecting the broader Southern California price surge during the pandemic years. However, compared to nearby markets like Riverside ($580,000+) or Corona ($700,000+), Moreno Valley still offers a meaningful entry point advantage. Distressed properties and off-market deals can often be found in the $350,000 to $420,000 range, creating realistic spreads for wholesalers and flippers working the 70% rule or better.

Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Moreno Valley

Not all neighborhoods in Moreno Valley carry the same investment potential. Some areas offer better rental yields, while others are prime territory for fix-and-flip activity. Here is a breakdown of the top zones to target.
Sunnymead Ranch and Centerpointe

These master-planned communities in the north and central parts of the city attract stable, working-class tenants and owner-occupant buyers alike. Homes here are generally well-maintained, which makes them better for buy-and-hold rental strategies. Expect median prices between $480,000 and $530,000, with single-family rentals fetching $2,400 to $2,800 per month.
March Air Reserve Base Adjacent Areas

The neighborhoods near March ARB on the southwest side of the city benefit from a consistent military tenant base. Military families often sign 12 to 24 month leases and qualify for BAH (Basic Allowance for Housing), which creates reliable rental income and lower vacancy rates. Investors who focus here often report vacancy rates under 4%.
West Moreno Valley and Edgemont

For fix-and-flip investors and wholesalers, the older housing stock in West Moreno Valley and the Edgemont area offers the best spread potential. Homes here were built in the 1960s through 1980s and often need updating. Purchase prices for distressed properties can dip to $340,000 to $380,000, with ARVs after renovation landing between $450,000 and $500,000 — giving skilled flippers a viable 15% to 20% gross margin.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Moreno Valley
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Moreno Valley because of the older housing inventory and motivated seller pool. Many homeowners in the area are long-time residents sitting on equity but facing deferred maintenance, probate situations, or financial stress. A typical wholesale deal in Moreno Valley might be contracted at $370,000 on a home with a $490,000 ARV, then assigned to a cash buyer for a $15,000 to $25,000 assignment fee. If you are new to the process, the Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide walks you through each step from finding the deal to closing the contract.
Fix and Flip

Flipping works well in Moreno Valley when buyers target the right properties. Cosmetic flips — new flooring, kitchen refresh, landscaping, and paint — tend to perform best because they keep renovation costs under $50,000 while still commanding top-dollar resale prices. Full gut rehabs are harder to pencil out given current ARVs and construction costs. Always run your numbers through a tool like the free Deal Calculator at AIWholesail before committing to any rehab budget.
Buy and Hold Rentals

Moreno Valley has a strong renter population — roughly 45% of households are renters — driven by affordability constraints and a young, growing workforce. Single-family homes in the $460,000 to $500,000 range are renting for $2,400 to $2,900 per month, producing gross yields of 6% to 7.5% annually. While that is not the double-digit cap rate territory of the Midwest, it is exceptional for Southern California and positions investors for long-term appreciation alongside cash flow.
Local Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Inventory remains tight: Moreno Valley typically carries 2 to 3 months of housing supply, keeping prices firm and competition high among buyers.
Logistics sector growth: Major warehouse and distribution expansion along the 215 freeway is bringing thousands of jobs, supporting population growth and rental demand.
Interest rate sensitivity: Higher mortgage rates have cooled retail buyer activity, which actually creates more motivated seller situations — a direct opportunity for cash investors.
New construction pressure: Several new home communities are being built in the eastern portions of the city, which may apply modest resale price pressure in those specific zip codes by 2025.
Rent growth stabilizing: After rapid rent increases from 2021 to 2023, rent growth has leveled off to a more sustainable 3% to 5% annually, which still supports solid long-term returns.

sections.content: The best real estate markets for investors are not the flashiest ones — they are the cities where jobs are growing, rents are stable, and prices still leave room to make a profit on day one. Moreno Valley checks all three boxes.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Moreno Valley

The best real estate deals in Moreno Valley CA rarely show up on Zillow or the MLS. Off-market properties — those sold directly by motivated sellers before they hit the open market — are where investors make their best margins. Direct mail to absentee owners, driving for dollars in older neighborhoods, and building relationships with local probate attorneys are all proven tactics. Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Moreno Valley

Out-of-state investors are active in this market, and with the right systems in place, distance is not a major obstacle. Before you commit capital, though, make sure you understand how to analyze real estate deals like a pro so you are not relying on gut instinct from 2,000 miles away.

items: Hire a local property manager before you close: Moreno Valley has several experienced property management companies familiar with the March ARB tenant pool and local rent ordinances. Budget 8% to 10% of monthly rent for management fees.

Get a local inspection and contractor network: Deferred maintenance is common in older Moreno Valley homes. Build a relationship with a licensed contractor and inspector who can walk properties on your behalf.

Understand California landlord-tenant laws: California is a tenant-friendly state with specific notice requirements, rent control considerations (though Moreno Valley does not currently fall under state rent control for single-family homes), and strict eviction procedures.

Use data, not emotion: Run every deal through a standardized analysis framework. Check ARV comps from the past 90 days within a half-mile radius, and always stress-test your assumptions with a 10% vacancy rate.

Tap into the local investor network: The Inland Valley Association of Realtors and local REIA groups host regular meetups where you can connect with wholesalers, title reps, and contractors who know the Moreno Valley submarkets well.

sections.content: When evaluating any Moreno Valley rental property remotely, request a neighborhood rental comp report from a local property manager before making an offer. They will tell you what the unit would actually rent for today — not what Zillow Rent Zestimate suggests.
